question.text: Copper becomes green when exposed to moist air for a long period. This is due to:

options.text: the formation of a layer of cupric oxide on the surface of copper.
the formation of a layer of basic carbonate of copper on the surface of copper.
the formation of a layer of cupric hydroxide on the surface of copper.
the formation of basic copper sulphate layer on the surface of the metal.

solution.text: Copper when exposed to moist air having $\mathrm{CO}_2$. It gets superficially coated with a green layer of basic carbonate $\mathrm{CuCO}_3$. $\mathrm{Cu}$ $(\mathrm{OH})_2$.
